learningObjective: Advance start by batch_size and let slicing clamp the final exclusive stop to the sequence length.

mechanismReview.pattern: Fixed-stride iteration with half-open sequence slices.
mechanismReview.recognitionCue: Examples must be emitted in bounded groups while preserving order and retaining a remainder smaller than the requested batch size.
mechanismReview.invariant: Before each yield, indices below start were yielded exactly once; the next slice covers [start,min(start+batch_size,n)), and the next start equals the previous requested stop.
mechanismReview.stateModel: Retain the input sequence, positive batch_size, moving start, and exclusive requested stop. Slicing itself handles the final boundary.
mechanismReview.visualRationale: An indexed array with stable start and stop markers shows half-open coverage, +batch_size movement, and why the final slice safely clamps.
rejectedAlternatives: Pre-drawn batch boxes hide the generator’s moving start and slice semantics.
A modulo grouping table complicates a direct stride-and-slice loop.
A full tensor diagram implies equal batch shapes and can conceal the short remainder.
mechanismReview.transferLesson: Use half-open slices and a fixed stride to partition ordered data exactly once; this transfers to pagination, chunked I/O, windowed inference, and streaming uploads.

mediumRationale: An original, problem-specific trace shows the actual input, changing state, safe transition, and result. The static first frame works without JavaScript; controls add step-by-step playback without replacing the proof with decoration.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would hide the exact data values and state changes that this problem needs.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the trace is a changing data state, so semantic HTML keeps values selectable, readable, and responsive.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Selected: each problem owns concrete frames rendered as arrays, maps, grids, trees, stacks, queues, intervals, pointers, bits, or tensor shapes.
mediumComparison.interaction: Selected as progressive enhancement: Play, Previous, Next, and step buttons reveal the same authored frames while static HTML remains complete.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the visual is an original synthesis of the supplied implementation and does not reuse source artwork.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: prose alone would make the learner simulate the changing data structure in working memory.
